_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Stop cached staging error pages from triggering recursive file preloads and excessive CPU use.
detail: Use staging public service settings directly instead of requesting the unshipped backend/secrets.json file that triggers the old cached fallback.
Start the offline-worker update before the page finishes loading, so recursive preloads cannot prevent the repair from installing.
Reject HTML responses requested as scripts or data, including old cached fallback pages with recursive preload headers.
Evict the invalid asset cache entry and retry the real file; preserve valid assets, offline downloads and learner progress.
Verified cached-HTML recovery, HTML rejection without preload headers, valid script caching and normal page navigation.

entries.summary: Clearer level help and a centred Smart Skip row
detail: Simplified level help around where to start, how Go sizes a batch, and what level progress means. Colour definitions can be expanded.
Smart Skip On uses a green selected state without a redundant tick.
Centred the compact controls and restored real skipped-word examples on desktop.

entries.summary: Explicit Off and On choices for Smart Skip
detail: Replaced the setup switch with Off and On buttons and a selected-state checkmark.
Desktop uses one line; mobile puts the skipped count and Details on a second line.
Removed the Recommended pill and example words from the setup row. Details still opens the individual options.
The control preserves the existing saved preference and recalculates the available cards.

entries.summary: Combine choosing a level with starting its next session
detail: The level picker, selected-level progress and Go controls share one Choose a level section.
Smart Skip sits in a separate compact row directly underneath.
The time choice appears on the left of Go; short batches keep the full-width Go button.
The level information modal now includes the session and progress explanation.

entries.summary: Show session batch sizes and a clear scrubber endpoint
detail: Go shows the number of new words in the selected batch, and the next-session heading names its level.
Future practice arrivals use smaller text; Practise keeps its plain button label.
Time choices hide for batches shorter than the saved duration permits. The selected duration stays saved.
The card scrubber shows the final position for every finite session, excluding temporary expression cards.

entries.summary: Portuguese: DeepSeek re-checked the 13,486 shakiest meanings on words 1–4,000 (temporary, labelled DEEPSEEK v25)
detail: Same cards and same examples as before; only the meaning shown on 13,486 example sentences changes.
Those picks come from DeepSeek, each confirmed by a second head-to-head check, ranked above the normal v25 picks.
Kept in a separate assigner file, not in the pipeline run, so a future normal v26 can outrank it.
Spanish and French bridge files now point at the new Portuguese release.

entries.summary: Keep imported known progress reviewable without invented answers
detail: The app and server use one review policy and repair answered stage-zero states.
Imported known cards have a separate 14-day review date, cleared by their next answer.
Stale device writes cannot reduce stored counts or replace newer answer dates.

entries.summary: Clearer companion cards and access to partly learned meanings
detail: Partly learned meanings remain selectable, including possible-meaning groups and identical short glosses.
Companion pills select the exact card, keep their own colours, and show a subtle share of uses beside frequency.
Rare-use numbers use the emphasis font without a circle; level labels above the cards are larger.

entries.summary: Grammar-word cards take less room, and a contraction's parts (al = a + el) sit beside the word
detail: The Grammar word badge now leads the role chips on one line; the separate badge row and the 'Used as' label are gone
Smaller chips and padding; at most 3 patterns; pattern meanings show only their first sense ('irse · to go away')
Dictionary notes such as 'Used other than figuratively…' and 'spelling of …' are no longer shown as a phrase meaning
'to / at' and 'to / at (+ verb)' show as one preposition chip
On contraction cards the a + el pill moves next to the word instead of its own line on the left
Measured at phone width: the block on al 126→63px, de 193→63px, se 298→116px, so the example sentence moves up

entries.summary: Compact star controls for saved phrases
detail: Moved saving to a star at the start of each expression, alongside the examples action, with Add to Saved confirmation.
Added a faint violet edge to expression boxes and a subtle star halo that remains visible when examples are closed.

entries.summary: Music workspace and saved phrases
detail: Choose artists, playlists and song subsets inside a full-screen Music workspace, then continue to study setup.
Keep words and phrases with their meanings, highlighted examples and translations in Saved. Revisit them from Progress or Settings, remove them or export a copy. Saving stays separate from review.

entries.summary: Cleaner centred passwordless sign-in
detail: One centred sign-in panel with full-width provider buttons and responsive spacing.
Added a temporary warning about iCloud and me.com email-code delivery. Microsoft is available alongside Google through Clerk.

entries.summary: Restored Joshua’s learning history to the new Google account
detail: The approved new Joshua identity receives the archived progress and history, keeping new onboarding preferences.
The replacement account retains its reviewer flagging controls. Other users’ archives are not restored.

entries.summary: Account creation starts with an empty username
detail: Removed all suggested usernames and the special case for the owner’s email address. Everyone enters their username explicitly.

entries.summary: Google and email-code accounts now open the main app
detail: New signed-in users choose a username once; their profile is bound to the verified Clerk account.
Staging and production use separate databases and account keys. Progress URLs are normalized before attaching session tokens.
Previous accounts and complete learning data are archived for manual restoration after the replacement accounts are created.

entries.summary: Google and email sign-in trial on the live Fluency address
detail: A separate sign-in check page uses the existing free Clerk development setup.
The trial verifies a real signed session with the isolated authentication API; it does not change or link existing progress.

entries.summary: Grammar-word cards for Spanish, Portuguese and Czech (and Dutch pronouns): function words shown by role and pattern, not a sense list
detail: Spanish (179 cards), Portuguese (198) and Czech (241) now show the 'Grammar word' block on function-word cards: articles, prepositions, conjunctions, pronouns, determiners, se/si. Each example carries its role or construction (gostar de, tener que, lo que, bát se).
Labels come from rules over a parser (Spanish: es_dep_news_trf; Portuguese, Czech: Stanza) plus Wiktionary. Hand-checked on random samples: about 95 percent right in each language.

Nothing else changed: every card, sense and example is identical to the live decks (pt v25 r4, es v25 r6, cs v22); new releases are the same decks with -fw1, and their side files (frequency, pools, cognates, merge lists, BRIDGE) are rebound copies.
Wording of role names is a draft for review.

entries.summary: Dutch prototype: pronouns and determiners now shown as grammar words too
detail: Dutch release nl-speech-cascade-proto2-6000x10: 150 cards get the 'Grammar word' block, up from 69. The 81 new ones are pronouns and determiners (je, ze, die, wat, mijn, haar, geen, alle, veel...).

Roles come from the parser: subject, object, possessive, reflexive (-self), question word, relative pronoun, pointing word, amount word. Glosses follow the sentence: 'ze' reads 'she' or 'they' from the verb.
Card summaries now keep one chip per role and gloss, so 'ze' shows both 'subject · she' and 'subject · they'.
Wording is a draft for review.

entries.summary: Grouped meaning rows centred again; front lemma capsule back to plain grey
detail: Back: rows that group several meanings (e.g. llevar's 'to take / to transport / to spend time on') no longer sit pushed to the right; an extra empty left column from today's ui-refinements.css is removed.
Front: the 'Verb from querer' capsule loses the POS-coloured outer ring and tint added in the same file; it is the neutral grey capsule again.
Cause: commit c3988450 (ui-refinements.css); no new overrides added.

entries.summary: Dutch prototype deck (CASCADE-WSD): function words shown as grammar words; other senses chosen by a cheap embedding + LLM cascade
detail: Dutch is enabled with release nl-speech-cascade-proto-6000x10 (6,000 cards, 10 examples each, published to Fluency-Releases-nl).

69 function words (de, het, een, van, op, aan, er, te, dat, als...) are labelled by rule, not WSD: the card back shows a 'Grammar word' block with 'Used as' roles and recurring patterns (aan het, om te, meegaan), and each example carries its role or construction label.
Other words: Qwen3-Embedding-4B picks the sense, e5-small checks it, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash decides the 34% where they disagree. Single-sense cards need no model.
Prototype wording ('Grammar word', 'Used as', 'Patterns') is a draft for review.

entries.summary: SHOWCASE: Tutorial copy tightened, Walkthrough unclipped & full-bleed on phones, About demo card alignment fixed
detail: Shortened tutorial explanations to <= 180 characters across Spanish, Portuguese, Czech, and French with no unreplaced placeholders.
Walkthrough modal is full-bleed on phones (<= 700px) with single-card scaling so cards are never clipped, even on 375x667.
Walkthrough pin labels support pinTitle ('How common') and pinAnchor ('.breakdown-trigger') so they never overlap headwords, context tags, or example sentences.
Fixed About modal demo cards (.about-demo-card) whose 3-column meaning rows were broken by global .meaning-row rules.
Updated About project button hint to 'A quick look at a card · about 30 seconds', accurate for both phone (3 screens) and desktop (2 screens).

entries.summary: Passwordless accounts on staging with Google and email codes
detail: Staging uses Clerk sign-in without password creation or guest mode.
Signed-in accounts save progress in a separate staging database, with server checks for account ownership.
Existing production accounts and progress are unchanged. Staging accounts start with empty progress.
Sign-up stays inside Fluency, with readable sign-in controls and a scrollable layout on small screens.

entries.summary: Simpler desktop navigation with Settings and Progress
detail: Remove the separate Your words shortcut from the desktop sidebar.
Keep Choose a set, Progress and Settings directly accessible, with Tutorial and Account below.
Settings retains its visible Study, App and Your words tabs.

entries.summary: Desktop sidebar for choosing sets, with a focused study view
detail: Desktop setup has a left sidebar for choosing sets, Your words, progress, tutorial, settings and account.
Settings, learning context and progress fill the workspace beside the sidebar; setup sheets no longer dock in the gutters.
Starting a set hides navigation and restores the existing study side panels. Returning to the main menu restores the sidebar.
Phones and narrow windows retain the compact top bar and dialogs.
Checked desktop setup, workspace navigation, study entry/exit and phone layout; app tests pass.

entries.summary: Clearer flashcards, lyrics and progress, with a preferred AI setting
detail: Tap companion lemma/POS pills on the front to switch readings; known meanings stay greyed and the front explains what remains to practise.
Brighter, lighter POS pills; aligned from labels; commonness appears before sense subrows and information follows them.
Larger artist photos and flags on progress screens; artist sources keep their own imagery.
Choose ChatGPT or Claude in Account settings and open its sign-in page; the preference chooses the lyric-view logo.
Larger English lyrics, level labels in study navigation and options, and word totals in the level scrubber.
Reuse the deployed Fλ icon throughout the app and give the startup language chooser a full-width placement.
Tutorial and unrelated in-progress edits are excluded from this staging commit.

entries.summary: The tutorial fills a phone screen: the card spans the full width and the explanation never moves the card
detail: Phone tutorial is full-bleed: no modal inset or rounded corners; title and exit share one row.
The tallest explanation's height is reserved once (measured at the coach's real width, including a chapter's two-button last note), so changing steps cannot move the card or the navigation.
A card that has to shrink is laid out at stage width ÷ scale, so it still spans the stage instead of sitting in a narrow strip; height cap raised to 760 px.
Work left uncommitted by the tutorial (SHOWCASE) chat; committed and staged on Josh's instruction after a phone-width smoke check.

entries.summary: Song translation: a play bar, tap-a-line to play, an English toggle, 389 more songs, and a tidier entity box
detail: Play bar at the bottom: previous line, play/pause, next line, and repeat this line. Repeat loops the line being sung, or the next one you tap. On a phone using Spotify's app, the highlight is kept in step by polling Spotify about every 1.5 s.
Tap anywhere on a line to play it from there (tapping a word still opens its card; the Spotify button still works).
EN button in the header hides or shows the English under each line; it is remembered on this device.

The song list grows from 30 to 419 songs: all of Bad Bunny, Rosalía and Young Miko in the lyrics release that LRCLIB has timed lyrics for (389 of 401). Search covers all of them; a song's lyrics are fetched when it is opened. 10 of them rest on a single LRCLIB record, so their timing is the least certain.
Song links now carry the song's Spotify id instead of its position in the list, so a saved link no longer shifts after importing a song. Old numeric links still open the song they used to.
Entity boxes are now a tight rectangle (4 px corners) that wraps the name, and the Wiktionary mark is a serif W at the start of the entity instead of the end.
Yonaguni's human translations load on the deployed site now: the build excluded the folder they were read from, so they never appeared there. They now match 51 of 60 lines.
Removed unused wiring: previous/next-song buttons, the compatibility anchors and the count badges.

entries.summary: Smart Skip is one line on every screen, and the level picker takes the language's (or artist's) colour
detail: Smart Skip on: the count moves up beside the name and the examples follow it, e.g. 'Smart Skip  3,115 skipped  e.g. idea, familia, minutos, importante, capitán'. The second 'N words skipped' line is gone.
At most five examples, set in the same type and colour as the level box's 'e.g.' line, and no trailing '...'. A narrow row shows fewer words, or none, rather than a cut-off list.

Phones get the same single line: name and Recommended badge when off, name and count when on (the 'Fewer cards, same coverage' line no longer has room and is dropped). Row height is 66px in every state; checked at 320, 375 and 800 wide in Speech and in Lyrics.
The selected level badge and its glow were fixed blue; they now use the language colour (Spanish red) or the artist's colour (Bad Bunny blue).

entries.summary: Song translation: catalogue songs now play from any line, the line being sung fills green, and the song list is just song and artist
detail: All 30 catalogue songs carry their Spotify track and LRCLIB line timing, baked offline (scripts/bake_probe_timings.py): 30 of 30 have a track, 29 of 30 have timing. Soso - Remix has no matching timed lyrics, so it stays plain with no play buttons.

While Spotify plays, the current line is highlighted and its words turn green as they are reached; finished lines dim. Word timing is estimated from each word's length within its line, because LRCLIB times lines, not words.

The view scrolls to the line being sung and stops following for four seconds when you scroll yourself. If Spotify is playing a different cut of the song (length differs by over 3 s) the highlight turns off and says so.
Songs with no Spotify track or no timing show no play buttons and no explanatory banner.
Song list shows only song and artist: the number, the line count, the ONLINE badge and the 'Curated Catalog' header are gone.
Yonaguni's human translations are matched to the timed lines by text (28 exact, more by near-match), so they no longer drift when the lines change.

entries.summary: Czech level coverage is now right for every level, and opening a deck does less repeated work
detail: Level coverage read each card's share under its dictionary form (ten) instead of the word actually spoken (to). Czech level 1 showed 32.0% of speech; it is 43.9%. Level 31 showed 0.9%; it is 0.3%.
Czech coverage now covers all 10,000 deck words (rebuilt from the same OpenSubtitles 2018 counts for release v22), so levels 31 to 100 show a figure.
Smart Skip works out its categories once per burst of work instead of about a dozen times when a deck opens: setup work on opening Czech ~800 ms to ~460 ms.
The hidden loading spinner no longer animates behind the app.
